key_sub: The signs of x, y and z decide the octant.
body_html:
How it works

  • Three axes meet at the origin O; the XY-, YZ- and ZX-planes divide space into eight octants.
  • A point on the x-axis is (a, 0, 0); a point in the XY-plane is (a, b, 0).
  • Distance between P(x1, y1, z1) and Q(x2, y2, z2): √((x2 − x1)² + (y2 − y1)² + (z2 − z1)²).
Example

Find the distance between (1, −3, 4) and (−4, 1, 2).

√((−5)² + 4² + (−2)²)

= √45

Answer: 3√5

Common mistakes

  • Leaving out the z-term in the distance formula.
  • Writing a point on the y-axis as (0, y, z).
  • Using the wrong signs for an octant.
